name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
summary: A seated cable vertical pull performed with a shoulder-width supinated grip to target the lats and biceps.

setup: Attach a straight or revolving lat bar to the high pulley of a pulldown machine.
Adjust the thigh pads so your lower body is firmly anchored with feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with an underhand (supinated) grip at approximately shoulder width.
Sit down under the pads, extending your arms overhead and tilting your torso slightly back from vertical.
steps: Depress your shoulder blades and pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your lats and biceps firmly as the bar approaches collarbone level.
Control the weight as you slowly extend your arms back overhead.
Allow your shoulder blades to elevate naturally at the top to achieve a full stretch before initiating the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the bar down to your chest and inhale as you return the bar with control to the overhead position.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso backward to create momentum.
common_faults.correction: Keep the torso stationary with a slight backward lean and initiate each pull strictly from the upper back and arms.

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbows wide out to the sides.
common_faults.correction: Track the elbows down and in front of the ribs to optimize the line of pull for the lats and protect the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the top.
common_faults.correction: Allow the arms to fully extend overhead so the lats experience a complete stretch on every repetition.

precautions: Ensure the thigh support is locked down securely to prevent the stack from pulling your hips off the seat.
